text:
mira: Heads-up — starting bring-up for customer 'Crescent' finetune. This is an LFA (low-rank fine-attach) adapter merged into main (PR: github.com/redwood/cust/crescent/merge/234). Running an int4 quant smoke + kv-cache sanity. Can someone sanity-check the quickpack prompts (invoices, dates, address extraction)? Thread will collect quick results and any tokenizer remap issues.

sam: On it. Quick q — is LFA a drop-in LoRA alias here or did you change the weight layout/token remap? I want to know if we need a conversion step before quant.

mira: LFA is intentionally different layout: adapter params live under adapter_blocks.v2 and we renamed a couple of special tokens -> tokenmap-v3. No conversion script yet, but the runtime supports an alias layer. Risk: tokenizer token id shifts causing numeric parse diffs.

lee: Ran a 500-sample quickpack against crescent-lfa:v1 int4. Topline: EM on invoice-id down 0.9pts vs baseline, but more worrying — date normalization errors for en-GB formats increased. Short log: 
```
input: "Invoice dated 12/11/24"
baseline: "2024-11-12"
crescent-lfa:int4: "2024-12-11"
```
Looks like day/month vs month/day flip for ambiguous dates.

mira: ack. Can you re-run with --kv-cache enabled? My hunch is prefix caching/position remap interacts with tokenmap-v3. Command we're using: 
```
r-infer eval --model crescent-lfa:v1 --quant int4 --prompts quickpack_invoices.json --kv-cache on --out /tmp/crescent_int4_kv.json
```
Also try hybrid int8-fp16 quant as a control.

deploy-bot: Canary job finished for crescent-lfa:v1 (canary id 3421) — 20k tokens processed, p50 65ms, p99 245ms, errors: 0.7% (most are parse diffs). Full logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/canaries/3421

jonah: I'll run a token-diff between baseline tokenizer and tokenmap-v3 and produce a small mapping patch if needed. If EM regression >1% we should have a rollback plan. Assigning follow-up to @sam and @lee to triage format-specific failures. :eyes: 

sam: Thanks — I'll also kick a quick eval with the new conversion shim (adapter_alias=true) to see if it closes the numeric swaps. If that fixes it, we can push a conversion step into the adapter loader.

mira: plan sounds good. If conversion shim helps, we'll schedule a dedicated quant-resweep (int4/int8/hybrid) and add the invoice/date prompts to the regression suite. Tagging this for the next eval-run: crescent-regression-pack-v1. :shipit:
